title: Pool-floor worktable view
purpose: Visual mockup only; no app code
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one additional camera view of a proposed immersive 3D portfolio website, landscape 1536x1024.
Input image 1 is the edit target and exact spatial/material reference: the existing fictional old swimming hall portfolio for Storm Selvig. Change the camera position, do not redesign the room.

Move the camera down onto the EMPTY DRY POOL FLOOR, beside the ordinary plywood worktable visible at far-left in the reference. Camera is at normal seated eye level, close enough that the desk and monitor occupy the left foreground and screen text is clearly readable. Orient the view across the same pool toward the right-hand wall with its three open changing-room doorways and upper gallery. All door thresholds remain raised on the surrounding walkway, the camera is clearly down below on the pool floor. The room is recognizable from the reference. Retain the long empty pool, imperfect grey/off-white tiles, faded green original waterline and floor markings, stainless steel rails, old timber, winter daylight, high windows and skylights, ceiling trusses, the upper gallery and its stairs. The tall changing-room door openings are reached from the surrounding walkway. Show the existing broad tiled steps as a visible return route toward foreground right. The far projection wall may remain partly visible. Maintain believable room continuity, proportions, materials and lived-in human specificity. This is a natural real-time 3D render of a website environment.

On the real monitor sitting on the plywood worktable, replace the picture thumbnails with a simple text-only page. Large plain black sans-serif lettering on an off-white screen, no illustrated project objects. Screen text must be legible and exactly:
"Projects"
"Smart Clock"
"UiASub RTOS"
"AI Dashcam"
"Studak"
"GodforsakenPlace"
"Open project"
Make the monitor size and camera distance allow these exact names to read cleanly. Keep the other ordinary desk objects modest and plausible.

Only small understated website overlays: top-left "Storm Selvig"; bottom-left "Back to walkway"; bottom-right "Index" and "Sound off". One small subtle white dot near the visible gallery stair hints at a route. No other overlay text.
Preserve the original naturally faded materials and winter light without imposing a branded colour palette. No giant props, invented project images, invented claims, hero headings, taglines, slogans, neon, people, game HUD, fantastical architecture, water, swimming activity or staged showroom polish. The visual should invite nonlinear exploration of the same tangible environment, at a quieter closer scale.

iterations.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied 1536x1024 pool-floor portfolio mockup. Make ONE targeted correction: the visible route back up to the walkway is missing. At the extreme lower-right foreground edge, show the near end of the broad original grey/offwhite tiled pool-entry steps with faded green step edges and one modest stainless steel handrail, rising out of the empty dry pool toward the right-hand surrounding walkway. The steps are partly cropped by the right frame edge but clearly recognizable as the return route from the pool floor. They should fit naturally with the existing architecture and should not obscure the desk, monitor, changing-room doors or gallery. These are ordinary worn pool-entry steps, not a floating staircase or a ladder. Keep absolutely everything else unchanged: camera at normal seated eye level, room layout, view direction, pool depth, desk and screen text, natural materials, winter light, projection, upper gallery, small white gallery dot, all overlay text and exact spelling. The monitor still reads exactly "Projects", "Smart Clock", "UiASub RTOS", "AI Dashcam", "Studak", "GodforsakenPlace", "Open project". Overlays remain top-left "Storm Selvig", bottom-left "Back to walkway", bottom-right "Index" and "Sound off". Natural real-time 3D render, no other changes.
iterations.reason: Restore the requested foreground return steps omitted in the initial view.
